key_headlines.title: South Korea's GDP Growth Forecast Raised to 3.5% for 2026
key_headlines.summary: Major international investment banks have consecutively raised Korea's economic growth forecast to 3.5% for this year, with next year's projection at 2.8%, driven by strong semiconductor exports and current account surplus.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Housing Prices Rise for Record 86 Consecutive Weeks
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyung-il expressed concern about Seoul apartment prices continuing to rise for an unprecedented 86 weeks, while announcing increased construction permits and groundbreaking (up 40% year-over-year) and plans to supply 1.19 million public housing units.

key_headlines.title: Youth Housing Crisis: Monthly Rent Over 1 Million Won for 9-Pyeong Rooms in Seoul
key_headlines.summary: Small studio apartments (under 30 square meters) with monthly rent exceeding 1 million won have increased sixfold over five years, with 1 in 8 Seoul officetel contracts exceeding 1 million won monthly rent, placing severe burden on young adults.

key_headlines.title: Trump Demands Compensation for Tariff Reduction on Korean Goods
key_headlines.summary: President Trump stated he requested compensation from South Korea in exchange for tariff reductions, amid discussions about Korea's 350 billion dollar investment commitment including the MASGA shipbuilding cooperation project.

key_headlines.title: Jeonse Fraud Victims to Receive Minimum One-Third of Deposits Starting November
key_headlines.summary: Beginning November 13, jeonse (lease deposit) fraud victims will be guaranteed recovery of at least one-third of their deposits through minimum support and advance payment programs, with applications processed by LH within 90 days.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economic performance continues to outperform expectations with major international investment banks raising the 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.5%, marking the sixth consecutive month of upward revisions. The government, led by Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyung-il, is focusing policy efforts on livelihood stabilization and enhancing potential growth rates through expanded housing and employment support. Key policy initiatives include supplying 1.19 million public housing units (77% in the Seoul metropolitan area) and strengthening small business and worker support programs. The government is also advancing Korea-US strategic investment and shipbuilding cooperation projects while promoting won internationalization and public sector reform.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's economic growth outlook has brightened considerably with eight major investment banks raising the 2026 GDP growth forecast to an average of 3.5%, continuing six consecutive months of upward revisions. The current account surplus is expanding faster than nominal GDP growth, with the surplus-to-GDP ratio projected at 17.5%, up 1.5 percentage points from the previous month. However, concerns persist about rising national debt, with Korea's debt-to-GDP ratio reaching 50%, comparable to major European economies facing fiscal instability. The government is implementing comprehensive livelihood policies including expanded public housing supply and strengthened support for workers and small businesses.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI opened at 6,860 points with a 1% decline despite positive US market performance and easing global government bond yields, as foreign and institutional investors engaged in simultaneous net selling. The KOSDAQ also showed weakness, though US indices hit record highs driven by third-quarter earnings expectations and declining US Treasury yields below 5.3%. Market focus remains on Samsung Electronics' third-quarter provisional earnings release, with analysts noting improved external conditions including eased European debt concerns. The Korean won traded at 1,350.6 won per dollar, down 7.8 won from the previous week's close.
sections.Industry & Technology: The battery industry is increasingly focusing on sodium-ion batteries (SIB) as a cost-competitive alternative to solid-state batteries for energy storage systems and affordable electric vehicles. POSCO Future M signed a six-year supply contract with Samsung SDI worth 6 trillion won for LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cathode materials, demonstrating strong demand for battery components in the EV market. Orient Precision successfully developed its own electric vehicle-specific polyurethane adhesive with high thermal conductivity, simplifying assembly processes and improving production efficiency. Hanwha's AI energy management system has been recognized as a next-generation technology by US trade publications for integrating power generation, storage, and consumption across all operational equipment.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment prices continue an unprecedented 86-week consecutive increase, prompting government concern about housing affordability despite implementing 40% more construction permits and groundbreaking between January and August compared to the previous year. Residential market recovery is extending beyond Seoul, with Ulsan showing declining unsold inventory and rising prices, supported by strong jeonse (lease deposit) values. The government designated five cities as unsold management zones in October, including newly added Osan and Gyeongsan, with existing Gangneung removed from the list. Interest rates and housing prices have shown an atypical positive correlation, defying conventional economic wisdom during periods of monetary tightening.
sections.International Economy: The US trade deficit reached 142 trillion won in August, the largest since Trump's tariff policies took effect, with projections showing the third consecutive quarter where trade deficits will reduce GDP by up to 2.5 percentage points. President Trump explicitly demanded compensation from South Korea in exchange for tariff reductions, citing Korea's recent 150 billion dollar investment commitment and pressure for the MASGA shipbuilding cooperation project. The US national debt has surpassed 5 quadrillion won, raising concerns about America's status as a global economic superpower amid rising government bond yields and fiscal uncertainty. Global government bond markets show instability, with US 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields reaching elevated levels, affecting international investment flows.
sections.AI & Economy: A 100-megawatt artificial intelligence data center is planned for Sejong National Industrial Complex, representing a 1.8 trillion won investment commitment to support Korea's AI infrastructure development. Economists generally express skepticism about AI's immediate large-scale job elimination, noting that young university graduates' unemployment issues represent longer-term trends since 2015 influenced by factors including graduate oversupply, remote work adoption, and high interest rates. The government is strengthening small business and startups' response to AI transformation through newly proposed regulatory innovation measures and support programs. Minister Lee So-young announced plans to advance SME global expansion based on Korean culture in beauty, food, and fashion sectors while implementing AI transition and carbon neutrality support programs.
sections.Others: Kiwoom Asset Management included Micron and SpaceX in its KIWOOM US AI Tech High Beta ETF during periodic rebalancing. Goldman Sachs projected increased volatility in Samsung Electronics on October 8 when the company releases third-quarter provisional earnings, citing overlapping selling factors. Mirae Asset Asset Management reported over 1 trillion won in individual purchases of its US Target Daily Covered Call ETFs tracking major US indices. Deputy Minister Kwon Dae-young apologized for investor losses from single-stock leverage ETFs, clarifying that final decisions on such products rest with the Financial Services Commission rather than the presidential office.
